---
title: "Chapter 2 — The Tribune's Gambit"
subtitle: "GM guide — Chapter 2"
---

*A Tribune arrives from Rome with sealed Senate orders. That night, Germanic raiders attack in force — with suspicious timing. The party must defend the fort, expose the Tribune's real agenda, and decide what to do with a man who might be right for all the wrong reasons.*

**Level:** 4 · **Players:** 5 (Iris, Julia Jana, Tanit, Rivia, Ursula) · **Time:** 3–4 hrs · **Type:** Mixed — RP-heavy investigation + combat

<details>
<summary>📁 The Story So Far</summary>

**Campaign position:** Session 2 of 5. Personal stakes (Session 1: retrieved a cursed divine weapon from a sealed vault) escalate to political. The party did their duty. The world has decided that doing their duty creates more problems, not fewer.

**What happened last session:**

- Party descended into a sealed vault on Corvinus' direct orders and retrieved the spear — the "God-Killer"
- Fought undead Roman warriors, two cultists of Mars, and one named cultist (Marius)
- Found evidence of an active Cult of Mars: OTHALAN contract token, binding scroll, active corruption
- Marius said something specific before dying — anyone who heard it carries that detail
- Sextus was on gate duty when they descended; he waved them through without issue

**What players currently believe:**

- They've done their duty and deserve answers about what they recovered
- Corvinus is the highest authority on this matter
- The cult is a local problem, probably manageable
- Sextus is alive and fine — a familiar face, a good soldier

**What they don't know yet:**

- Sextus is dead
- The Tribune is already an hour out from the fort
- Vercingetorix has been watching the fort for days
- Quintus Flavius (the killer) is already inside the Tribune's entourage

**Open threads coming in:**

- What is the spear, really? Where did it come from?
- Who sent the cultists? "Marius" is a name, not an answer
- Why is Cassia barely sleeping?

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 The Truth Behind the Session</summary>

**What is actually going on:**

Senator Gaius Cassius Brutus learned via Aldric and other informants that a divine weapon was unearthed at Vindolanda. He knows what the spear is — in the right hands it gives the Emperor unprecedented frontier legitimacy. He cannot allow that. He sent Tribune Lucius — his son by blood, not name — with genuine Senate authority (orders signed by a compliant consul) to retrieve and destroy the artifact before it reaches Rome.

Quintus Flavius, a pre-positioned sleeper agent embedded in the fort's garrison for six months, was supposed to steal the spear the night before. Sextus caught him at the storage chains. Quintus killed him and fled with the Tribune's arriving entourage, hiding in plain sight. The Tribune may not know Quintus personally — he is Brutus' tool, not Lucius'.

**NPC schedules — what happens if players do nothing:**

- Tribune Lucius: Arrives, claims authority, demands spear in his quarters by hour 2, demands Corvinus relieved by hour 3, departs within 36 hours
- Vercingetorix: Raid begins at nightfall regardless — the spear's reawakening was felt by spirit-sensitive warriors across three tribes
- Cassia: Spends the day watching the Tribune from the shrine doorway, documenting everything, saying nothing until after the raid
- Quintus Flavius: Departs with the Tribune's escort under cover of morning chaos; never seen again in Session 2 unless identified
- Aldric: Watches, sends one report north before the party leaves

**What changes if players do nothing:**

Tribune departs with the spear by dawn. Cassia cannot stop him. Varro cannot legally stop him. Session 3 begins with the party either following on orders or adrift with no objective. Vercingetorix's raid still happens — he reaches the principia to find the spear gone. He becomes an enemy for Session 3.

**The session's central tension:**

Roman legal authority (real orders, genuine Senate power) vs. the truth of what that authority is actually doing (destroying a divine artifact for a corrupt senator). The party has been trained to follow orders. This is an order they should not follow.

**Escalating stakes:**

- **Personal:** Any character who touched the spear is already dreaming. If the Tribune gets it, those dreams are someone else's problem — or the corruption stays with the last holder.
- **Local:** If Vercingetorix is killed or alienated, the frontier relationship with three Germanic tribes breaks permanently. Understaffed fort. Increased raids.
- **Faction/Regional:** If the spear reaches Rome under Brutus' control, he destroys it privately. The party are the only people in position to stop this.
- **World/Cosmic:** The spear's destruction ritual requires a specific grove and a willing sacrifice. If it's destroyed wrong, the curse passes to whoever is nearest when it breaks.

**Pre-session secrets — ask privately before play:**

- *For whoever touched/held the spear in Session 1:* "Your character dreams of standing in the principia alone, the spear in your hands, a voice that isn't yours speaking your name. When you wake — do you tell Cassia, or hold it until you're certain?"
- *For Julia Jana (Cleric/Twilight):* "You've been aware all night that something in the fort's divine space is crowded. A presence that wasn't here before. Does Julia share this, or hold it until she's certain?"
- *For Tanit (Bard/Charlatan):* "Someone in the Tribune's entourage — a young aide, finely dressed — recognized you and looked away too quickly. Does Tanit know who that is, or is it a mystery she's choosing to ignore?"

</details>

**Pacing:** Cold Open 10 min · Scene 1 30 min · Scene 2 45–60 min (investigative heart, the session breathes here) · Scene 3 45–60 min (kinetic peak) · Scene 4 20–30 min (emotional peak). Never let Scene 2 run longer than Scene 3.

**The through-line:** "The law says one thing. The truth says another. Which do you follow, and what does that make you?"

**Guy Sanders structure check:**
- Scene 0/1 hooks immediately (murder + authority disruption before breakfast)
- Scene 2 reframes everything (Tribune = Brutus' agent, not the Senate's honest arm)
- Scene 3 puts real pressure on (combat forces Vercingetorix decision in real time)
- Scene 4 resolves Session 2's central tension and opens Session 3's question

**Convergence:** All investigation paths (Scene 2) converge at Scene 3 regardless. What the party carries into Scene 4 determines their leverage — not whether they can act.

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 0 — Cold Open: Dead Sentry (RP)</summary>

*The morning before the Tribune arrives. North gate. Sextus — the sentry with the bad knee who always complained about the cold — lies with his throat open and his eyes still surprised.*

**Players know:** They retrieved the spear last session · **Players don't know:** The killer is already in the entourage arriving at the south gate

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Establish that someone inside the walls is a threat; force the party to hold an unsolved murder while an entirely new crisis walks through the gate |
| **Player objective** | Investigate the body; start working out who did this |
| **Key reveal** | Sextus was killed by someone he didn't read as a threat — someone he knew |
| **Key mechanic** | Perception DC 11; Medicine DC 13; Investigation DC 14; Survival DC 12 |
| **Beat 1** | Varro crouches beside the body, voice quiet: *"This was done by someone who knew his patrol route. Someone inside the walls."* |
| **Beat 2 — THE MOMENT** | The south gate trumpet sounds — three long notes. Visitors on the road. The murder is not resolved. It is now competing with something else. |
| **Beat 3** | They cannot finish this investigation now. The world has moved on. They carry this unresolved into Scene 1. |
| **XP / reward** | 50 XP per clue found here (max 150 XP) |
| **If they skip** | Varro tells them later. The clues remain available in Scene 2 if they return. |
| **Three clues** | ① Sextus faces the wall he was supposed to watch — he wasn't surprised from behind (Perception DC 11) · ② Boot print in mud: legionary-issue, small size, heavy inside-heel wear — left toward stables (Survival DC 12 or Investigation DC 14) · ③ ROMA CADIT carving uses angular Germanic runic strokes, not Roman cursive (Arcana DC 13 passive — Rivia auto) |
| **Handouts** | None |

<details>
<summary>📄 Read Aloud</summary>

> *Dawn. Someone is shaking you awake before the trumpet sounds.*
>
> *Outside, a cluster of soldiers stands at the north gate. At their feet, Sextus — the sentry with the bad knee who always complained about the cold — lies with his throat open and his eyes still surprised. No tracks. No blood trail. No explanation.*
>
> *Centurion Varro crouches beside the body. He looks up at you. His voice is very quiet:*
>
> *"This was done by someone who knew his patrol route. Someone inside the walls."*
>
> *He points to the carving in the wood.*
>
> *Before anyone can speak — a trumpet call from the far side of the fort: three long notes. Visitors on the road.*
>
> *Through the south gate, riders in gleaming armor approach.*

*(Passive Perception ≥ 11: Sextus is facing the wall he was supposed to be watching. He did not turn toward the threat. He let the attacker close.)*

*(Passive Arcana ≥ 13 — Rivia: The ROMA CADIT carving uses angular runic strokes, not Roman cursive. A Roman writing Latin would use rounded forms. Someone with Germanic inscriptional practice made this.)*

</details>

<details>
<summary>📄 NPC Appearance & Presence</summary>

**Tribune Lucius Valerius Maximus**
- **Look:** Late twenties. Lean, deliberate build. Olive complexion, precisely cut dark hair.
- **Wearing:** Traveling cloak with senatorial purple trim; rings on every finger — one crest-ring, three ornamental, one plain iron band, tarnished, sized down, not made for him.
- **Posture:** Walks like the space belongs to him and will be vacated accordingly. Never looks back.
- **One memorable detail:** The iron ring on his right index finger. It doesn't match. Insight DC 14: he wears it to remember something, not to display it.
- **First impression line:** *"He doesn't look at the fort as a place people live. He looks at it as a problem to be processed."*

**Quintus Flavius** (somewhere in the entourage — hard to single out)
- **Look:** Forties. Mid-height, legionary-standard build. Close-cropped greying hair. Unremarkable.
- **Wearing:** Frontier soldier's traveling gear, clean enough.
- **Posture:** Walks like a legionary who already knows the layout. Never asks for directions.
- **One memorable detail:** He already knows which way to go. Perception DC 15 (active, watching the entourage specifically): he orientates toward the stables, not the barracks.
- **First impression line:** *"He holds his shoulders wrong for a servant. You've seen that posture on gate sentries."*

</details>

<details>
<summary>📄 NPC Awareness — Scene 1</summary>

**Tribune Lucius**
- **Right now:** Moving into principia, issuing rapid orders, writing Corvinus' suspension order
- **Knows:** The spear's location; party names (from Corvinus' advance communication); raid is tonight (Brutus told him — he's been told to secure the spear before it hits)
- **Triggered by:** Party mentioning "the seal date" on Handout 4 → no answer. Party saying "Brutus" by name → goes very still.
- **If never engaged:** Completes extraction plan; departs at dawn with the spear.

**Quintus Flavius**
- **Right now:** Moving through entourage, checking stable exits, assessing the party from a distance
- **Knows:** He killed Sextus; he is the sleeper agent; Varro suspects something
- **Triggered by:** Anyone examining the entourage specifically (Perception DC 15) → party sees him orienting wrong
- **If never identified:** Departs with entourage; surfaces in Session 4 as potential *Frumentarius* contact

</details>

<details>
<summary>📄 Handouts — Scene 1</summary>

**Handout 4 — Tribune's Sealed Orders**
- **Physical:** Heavy parchment, folded in thirds, eagle-crest Senate wax seal. Expensive paper — meant to be kept.
- **Trigger:** Tribune formally presents credentials to Corvinus and slides the document forward. Let a player break the seal.
- **Handoff narration:** *"He holds it out without looking at you. 'Have someone literate verify the seals.'"*
- **Reveals without check:** Genuine Senate authority. Corvinus' command suspended. Party elevated to Special Envoy status.
- **Skill check adds:** Investigation DC 13 — the counter-seal on the reverse is dated six weeks before any official notification of the spear's recovery. These orders were prepared before Rome officially knew.
- **Connects forward:** If party cites the seal date in Scene 4 ("these orders were dated before Rome knew"), the Tribune has no answer. One round of credibility gone.

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 2 — Investigation Window (Exploration / RP)</summary>

*Three hours between the Tribune's arrival and nightfall. The fort is tense in the way a watch-spring is tense: not loud, just loaded.*

**Players know:** Tribune has legal authority; something is wrong; they have time to investigate
**Players don't know:** The encoded letter; Aldric's intelligence role; Brutus' identity

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Give the party agency. Everything found here they carry into Scene 4. Nothing is wasted. Nothing is required. |
| **Player objective** | Discover who the Tribune really serves |
| **Key reveal** | Tribune Lucius is working for Senator G.C.B. — Gaius Cassius Brutus — not for the Senate's legitimate interest |
| **Key mechanic** | Stealth DC 13 or Deception DC 14 (Tribune's quarters); Investigation DC 16 or Thieves' Tools DC 14 (dispatch box); Insight DC 18 (Aldric); History DC 13 passive (G.C.B. identity) |
| **Beat 1** | Three investigation paths open simultaneously: Tribune's quarters, the shrine (Cassia), Centurion Varro |
| **Beat 2 — THE MOMENT** | Finding and beginning to decode the letter. Or: Varro drops the political act — *"That Tribune was posted to the financial investigation commission six months ago. Start with which senators have frontier contracts."* |
| **Beat 3** | Whatever they've found, the sky is dark. The drums start. |
| **XP / reward** | 200 XP for successful entry and search of Tribune's quarters. 100 XP for accessing any one clue path. Bonus 50 XP for finding and decoding the letter. |
| **If they skip** | Scene 3 happens regardless. Scene 4's Persuasion DC stays at 17 instead of dropping to 14. The party negotiates from no evidence. |
| **Three clues** | ① Encoded letter in Tribune's quarters (entry + dispatch box) · ② Tribune's behavior during the raid in Scene 3 (Perception DC 14 / Insight DC 14) · ③ Ask Varro directly — no check, he volunteers the financial commission posting |
| **Handouts** | Handout 5 — successful dispatch box search |

- **Knows:** Party's departure direction (he asked around this morning), spear's current location, Tribune's arrival status

Investigation DC 14 (searching his room) → cipher note in same letter-shift format as Handout 5, addressed north, signed with a raven-claw symbol.

<details>
<summary>📄 Handouts — Scene 2</summary>

**Handout 5 — Encoded Letter**
- **Physical:** Tea-stained paper, folded twice, different stock and handwriting from Handout 4. *"Caesar cipher, shift 3"* written faintly on the reverse.
- **Trigger:** Successful dispatch box search (DC 16 Investigation or DC 14 Thieves' Tools).
- **Handoff narration:** *"Inside the box, under the official correspondence: a single sheet on cheaper paper. More personal. The handwriting is careful — someone who encrypts by habit."*
- **Reveals without check:** Cipher text. Players decode by shifting each letter three forward. Plaintext: *"The artifact must not reach Rome. By any means necessary. Our mutual friend's ambitions depend on its permanent removal. You know what to do. — G.C.B."*
- **Skill check adds:** History DC 13 (Julia Jana / Tanit / Rivia auto) — "G.C.B." = Gaius Cassius Brutus. Republican rhetoric. Enormous wealth. Frontier military contracts. Known motive.
- **Connects forward:** This letter reduces Scene 4's Persuasion DC from 17 → 14. With it in hand, the party is proving, not pleading. Also: the cipher format matches the raven-claw note in Aldric's room.

</details>

<details>
<summary>📄 Three Clues — Exposing the Tribune</summary>

**The reveal:** Tribune Lucius is working for Senator Gaius Cassius Brutus. His mission is to prevent the spear reaching Rome — not to deliver it. The Senate orders are real. His purpose is not.

---

**Clue ①** — The Encoded Letter *(direct action — requires entry + search)*

Stealth DC 13 (past Praetorian guard) or Deception DC 14 (claim authorization for security inspection — Tanit can do this automatically given the written order). Inside: Investigation DC 16 to find the box, or Thieves' Tools DC 14 to open it directly. Cassia can identify the cipher format if shown the letter — she's seen similar Senate correspondence.

---

**Clue ②** — Tribune's Behavior During the Raid *(fires in Scene 3)*

Watch him specifically during the alarm. Perception DC 14 (active: tracking his movements when the horn sounds) or Insight DC 14 (reading his face). He moves immediately to the principia — not the walls. His Praetorians follow without being ordered to. They're protecting the spear room, not the fort. Afterward, Tribune pushes to accelerate departure, citing "raider intelligence." Varro: *"Defenders defend the people. They defended the artifact. Ask yourself why."*

---

**Clue ③** — Varro's Network *(no check, ask directly)*

Ask Varro about the Tribune. No roll required — he volunteers: *"That Tribune was posted to the financial investigation commission six months ago. Guess who was embezzling? Start with which senators have frontier contracts."* History DC 13 (Julia Jana / Tanit / Rivia auto): "G.C.B." points to Gaius Cassius Brutus.

</details>

<details>
<summary>📄 Encounter Details — The Great Raid</summary>

## Scale

Total raiding force: ~120 warriors. The party covers their assigned wall section (~25 enemies reach them). Three other sections run on NPC background rolls. The fort is outnumbered — the question is whether you hold long enough.

**Garrison (realistic, 40% strength of 480):** ~190 defenders total spread across the full perimeter. The party's section: ~15 NPC soldiers plus the party. Every round without a breakthrough is a win.

|---|---|---|
| `Goblin_Skirmisher.rptok` | 12 | Zone 9 suppression fire; Nimble Escape each round, never same position |
| `Orc_Raider.rptok` | 8 | Frontline shock — Aggressive closes 60ft/turn, cannot be kited |
| `Hobgoblin_Warrior.rptok` | 8 | Ladder assault; hold wall for formation, then Martial Advantage |
| `Druid.rptok` | 2 | Zone 9 chanting buff (+1 ATK all raiders) + Fog Cloud / Entangle |
| `Ogre.rptok` | 1 | West gate ram — 3d6+4/round automatic; gate falls round 4 if untouched |
| `Worg.rptok` | 2 | Released alongside orcs; bite + knock prone DC 13 STR |

## Background Battle — NPC Sections

Roll each round. GM narrates what players can hear.

| Section | Roll | DC | Narrative on failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| North wall (east half) | d20+4 | 13 | Horn signal, shouting in Germanic — goblins on the north parapet |
| East wall | d20+3 | 13 | Fire arrow lands in the barrack roof. Someone screaming |
| South approach | d20+5 | 13 | Held — no news from there |

**Two consecutive failures = section breached.** Torchlight moves inside the fort from that direction. Hard choice: hold your position or reinforce. NPC section defenders will hold their ground regardless — only the party can choose to abandon their post.

## Archer / Ranged PC Spotlight

Ranged characters are **essential** in a siege. This is their session.

**Elevation Advantage:** Any ranged attack from the wall or rampart against targets at or below wall height = **ADVANTAGE**. Open field, targets clearly visible. This is the single biggest siege bonus — ranged PCs have advantage on most attacks in Phases 1–2.

**Suppression Fire (action):** Choose a 10ft zone. Enemies entering or moving through it this round make CON save DC 12 or must use Dash as their action. Stops ladder climbers and orc charges for one round. Goblin archers in zone 9 can be suppressed (they can't hide AND advance).

**Called Shots (specific target, declare before rolling):**
- **Ogre's hands:** Hit → Ogre has disadvantage on gate damage roll this round (advantage against gate tracker HP).
- **Druid Concentration:** Hit → Druid makes Concentration check DC 10 + damage dealt. This is the most important action available to a ranged PC in Phases 1–2.
- **Goblin signal-caller:** Perception DC 13 to spot one goblin giving arm signals. Kill it → WIS DC 10 for all goblins in 30ft radius or they auto-flee.

**Crossfire:** Two ranged PCs fire at the same target in the same round → both roll at **ADVANTAGE**.

## Leader / Charisma PC Spotlight

**RALLY (action) — Tanit, Julia Jana:** Charisma DC 12. On success: 3 adjacent NPC soldiers gain 8 temp HP and advantage on their next attack. Druid chanting actively suppresses this (DC 14 Religion to recognise counter-chanting — then killing a druid restores the rally bonus).

**TACTICAL COMMAND (action, any PC):** Intelligence (History) or Insight DC 10. Direct 2 NPC soldiers this round as your bonus action — they act on your target.

**COVER! (reaction, Perception DC 12):** Warn an adjacent ally of an unseen attack. That ally may use their reaction to halve damage from that hit.

**INSPIRE (Bard bonus action):** Bardic Inspiration die applied to any NPC section's background roll this round. On a high roll, that section holds even without it.

**FOCUS FIRE (free shout, once/round):** No action cost. Point out a high-value target. All allies who attack that target this round roll at advantage.

## Tactical AI

- **Goblin Skirmishers:** After every shot, hide (Stealth +6). New cover position. If 3+ killed same round: remaining goblins within 30ft make WIS DC 10 or flee. Never engage melee.
- **Hobgoblin Warriors:** Wait for two to be on the wall before attacking. Formation matters more than speed. Longsword (two-hand) once established, re-equip shield as bonus action next round.
- **Orc Raiders:** Aggressive every turn. If Relentless Endurance triggers: visible moment — show the party the orc stand back up. Next attack with advantage (enraged). Then any hit drops it.
- **Bugbear Ambushers:** Stay hidden until round 3-4. Reveal from east (party facing west). Surprise Attack opener. Target: PC who looks most dangerous. Then grapple-drag if morningstar hits. Primary goal: wall attrition, not kills.
- **Ogre:** Gate only. 2-3 sustained ranged hits from east = looks east for 1 round (gate not rammed). Otherwise: Gate. Gate. Gate.
- **Druids:** Concentration priority. If Fog Cloud broken: Entangle. If Entangle broken: Hold Person on party's best melee. Below 10 HP: flee treeline immediately.
- **Vercingetorix:** Does not attack first. Walks toward principia. Body-blocked (grapple or just standing in way): stops and talks. Words without steel: walks through. He respects demonstrations of capability, not threats.

9. Worgs / Dire Wolves — 5

<details>
<summary>📄 Vercingetorix — Trust Track</summary>

*This is the most important NPC mechanic in Sessions 3–4. Set the trust level here.*

| Trust level | What he'll share in Session 3 |
|---|---|
| **None** (fought and killed him, or ignored him) | Nothing — use his lieutenant (Arnulf, Gladiator stat block, same knowledge, one additional exchange to reach Complete Trust) |
| **Low** (treated as enemy, stopped fighting) | *"The spear has a name in my language. It means 'the thing that should not exist.' My grandfather helped seal it."* |
| **Medium** (talked, acknowledged his people's claim) | Above, plus: *"It cannot be destroyed anywhere except a specific grove. One day's march into the Teutoburg Forest. My people know the way."* |
| **High** (openly respected, treated as an equal) | Above, plus: *"The ritual requires a willing sacrifice. Not blood. Something real. The grove knows the difference."* |
| **Complete trust** (proved by action) | Above, plus: *"I am dying. I have perhaps a year. I chose this campaign because of the spear. If you destroy it, my people's three-generation wound closes. That is enough for me."* — Full ally for Sessions 3–4. |

**Earning trust in Scene 3 (social paths — player chooses approach):**
- **Persuasion DC 14** (acknowledging his people's legitimate claim): Standard path.
- **Intimidation DC 14** (controlled display of martial competence — not a threat, a demonstration that you understood how he fights and chose not to kill him): He responds to *audacia*, not threats. On success: *"You fight well for a Roman."* Immediately moves to Medium trust.
- **Insight DC 13** (reading that he's assessing, not negotiating, and responding to the assessment itself): Jumps one trust level on first successful exchange.

**His voice:**
- *"Romans name everything they find. That is how they believe they own it."*
- *"I have been dying from a sickness for two years. I fight anyway. Your spear will not frighten me."*
- *"Your fort smells of fear. My camp smells of wood smoke. Fear is the worse smell."*
- *"I came for the God-Killer. I did not come for you."*

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 4 — The Tribune's Move (RP / Decision)</summary>

*The courtyard is full of wounded soldiers, and the Tribune walks through it like it's a corridor.*

**Players know:** Everything from Scenes 0–3; evidence level varies by what they found
**Players don't know:** The specific accusation; Corvinus' angle; that Varro has been ready for this

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Force an irreversible choice. No right answer. This is the session's emotional peak. |
| **Player objective** | Navigate the Tribune's accusation without ending up in chains, dead, or fugitives — unless they choose to be |
| **Key reveal** | Corvinus and the Tribune briefly align against the party. Varro does not. |
| **Key mechanic** | Insight DC 14 (during accusation, window closes when speech ends); Persuasion DC 17 / DC 14 with evidence; Intimidation DC 15 |
| **Beat 1** | Tribune appears — immaculate — in the blood-soaked courtyard. "Arrest them." |
| **Beat 2 — THE MOMENT** | *"I concur with the Tribune's assessment,"* says Corvinus. Then: *Varro takes a slow step to stand beside the party. His hand moves to his gladius. "Do you," he says.* |
| **Beat 3 — CLOSING IMAGE** | Party acts. Do NOT resolve the consequence fully — let the closing image hang. Varro's hand. The Praetorians. The Legate's face. |
| **XP / reward** | 600 XP for navigating Scene 4 without full surrender or TPK. 300 XP for surrender (they survived). |
| **If they skip** | Cannot be skipped |
| **Three clues** | ① Insight DC 14 during accusation speech (window closes when speech ends) · ② Evidence in hand (letter, seal date) → DC drops 17 → 14 · ③ Varro's position — passive, no roll — he's already there |
| **Handouts** | None |

> *He looks at the carnage with mild professional interest.*
>

>
> *He turns to the Praetorians. "Arrest them."*
>

>

<details>
<summary>📄 Decision Point — All Options</summary>

| Option | How | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **Expose the Tribune** | Produce the decoded letter or cite the seal date | Praetorians hesitate. Varro moves. Tribune trapped. Session 3 politically complicated but party free. |
| **Negotiate** | Persuasion DC 17 (DC 14 with evidence) | Tribune offers private deal: *"Help me destroy it my way and I'll make this go away."* |
| **Intimidate** | Intimidation DC 15 (controlled — you've survived things he hasn't; delivered calmly, not angrily) | DC 15: Praetorians hesitate; Tribune calculates; offers the deal from a weaker position. DC 20: Praetorians disengage without a direct order. He knows the party has leverage. |
| **Fight** | Tribune + 6 Praetorians (CR 2 each) + Varro and 6 veterans on party's side | Extremely dangerous. Win = fugitives from Rome. |
| **Flee with Vercingetorix** | He's visible or nearby; party treated him with respect in Scene 3 | Forest refuge. Fugitives with a powerful Germanic ally. Session 3 opens in his camp. |
| **Surrender** | Give up the spear | Confined to quarters. Session 3 as prisoners escorted to Rome. |

**Temporal gate — Tribune's doubt:**

One round. One check. Window closes when he finishes his accusation speech.

- Insight DC 14: He hesitates before "enemies of Rome." His eyes flick to Varro.
- What it opens: Negotiation DC drops from 17 → 14. The party can invoke the hesitation: *"You paused. You know this isn't true."*
- Why the window closes: Once he finishes and walks the words back, the doubt sealed over. Catching him before the choice became a fact is the point.

**Praetorian Guard** ×6 (if combat) — CR 2 · 450 XP each

> **AC** 18 · **HP** 52 (8d8+16) · **Speed** 30 ft
> **Longsword** +5 to hit. *Hit:* 7 (1d8+3) slashing. Shield bash bonus action (STR DC 12 or prone).

Tactical AI: Fight in pairs, protect Tribune first. If Tribune falls unconscious or orders retreat → they disengage. They do not fight to the death for a bluffed mission.

**Secondary objective (if combat):** Capture the Tribune alive. Killing him makes permanent enemies of Rome. Capturing him gives Session 3 leverage.

<summary>📁 Session Close & Consequences</summary>

**How the session ends (by path):**

| Session 2 ending | Closing image | Session 3 opening |
|---|---|---|
| Tribune exposed, arrested | Party free, politically exposed. Legate temporarily back in command. Not grateful. | Party leaves fort under own terms — but Rome knows their names. |
| Negotiated deal | Tribune nods. *"We'll discuss terms in the morning."* | Uneasy alliance. Tribune travels with the party. |
| Fought the Praetorians | Through the gate. Vercingetorix's torches ahead in the forest. | 12 hours later, in the forest. Vercingetorix found them at the treeline. |
| Fled with Vercingetorix | Forest. His camp. Roman soldiers in a Germanic war camp. Safe only because he said so. | Two miles north. Negotiating position depends on Session 2 trust level. |
| Surrendered | The clank of chain. A Praetorian collecting weapons, politely. | Prisoners escorted to Rome. Six days. The spear in a sealed crate ahead. |

**Consequences to track:**

- Vercingetorix trust level set: None / Low / Medium / High / Complete
- Decoded letter found or not: Scene 4 Persuasion DC 17 or 14
- Quintus Flavius identified or not: Frumentarius advancement trigger met or pending (surfaces Session 4)
- Aldric caught or not: Session 3 chieftain has advance notice of party's approach (or doesn't)
- Varro survived the raid or not: Scene 4 DCs at normal or +3 (Cassia covers some of his role if lost)
- Bog valerian request noted or not: Session 3 Nature check opportunity exists (or Cassia's rites run at half capacity Session 4)
- Corruption tracking: Any character who held/attuned the spear dreams tonight. Before Scene 3 fires, ask the highest-corruption player to describe their dream to the table.

**Transition hook:** Wherever they end up — what do they do about the spear now? And who, exactly, is G.C.B.?

**Debrief question:** "Your character had a moment tonight when the law said one thing and their instincts said another. Which one did they follow — and do they think that was the right call?"
